items.title: DeepSeek-v4.1-Flash-1017
items.body:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. Alongside these gains, the model reduces task execution time and output length, enabling users to complete tasks faster and at lower cost and advancing the performance–cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses.

† denotes the text-only subset of HLE. We use the Claude Code harness for Terminal-Bench 4.0 and the Mini-SWE-V2 harness for DeepSWE v1.1.

This release does not include a Jinja-format chat template. The encoding folder contains a self-contained Python reference implementation (encoding.py) with test cases for multi-turn conversations, tool calling, thinking mode, numeric reasoning effort, mid-conversation system messages, and interleaved image content.

For production use, we additionally release deepseek-recipe, a set of Rust libraries with Python bindings that provides the same prompt format as a maintained, protocol-aware toolkit. It converts Messages, Chat Completions, and Responses API requests into the Conversation format, encodes them into DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 prompts or token IDs, and parses model output back into complete or streamed responses — covering thinking, tool calls, images, and generation settings. Model inference, tool execution, and HTTP transport are left to the caller.

Please refer to the inference folder for instructions on weight conversion and running inference locally.

Recommended sampling parameters:

items.body_ko:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017은 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash의 마이너 업데이트로, 추론, 코딩, 에이전트 작업 및 시각 벤치마크 전반에 걸쳐 상당한 개선을 제공합니다. 이러한 향상과 더불어 모델은 작업 실행 시간과 출력 길이를 줄여 사용자가 더 빠르고 저렴한 비용으로 작업을 완료할 수 있도록 하며, 여러 에이전트 하네스에서 성능-비용 파레토 곡선을 발전시킵니다.

†는 HLE의 텍스트 전용 하위 집합을 나타냅니다. 우리는 Terminal-Bench 4.0에 Claude Code 하네스를 사용하고 DeepSWE v1.1에 Mini-SWE-V2 하네스를 사용합니다.

이 릴리스에는 Jinja 형식의 채팅 템플릿이 포함되어 있지 않습니다. 인코딩 폴더에는 다중 턴 대화, 도구 호출, 사고 모드, 수치 추론 노력, 대화 중 시스템 메시지 및 인터리브된 이미지 콘텐츠에 대한 테스트 케이스가 포함된 자체 포함 Python 참조 구현(encoding.py)이 있습니다.

프로덕션 사용을 위해, 우리는 또한 deepseek-recipe를 릴리스합니다. 이는 유지 보수되고 프로토콜 인식 도구 키트와 동일한 프롬프트 형식을 제공하는 Python 바인딩이 있는 Rust 라이브러리 세트입니다. 이는 Messages, Chat Completions 및 Responses API 요청을 Conversation 형식으로 변환하고, 이를 DeepSeek V4 및 V4.1 프롬프트 또는 토큰 ID로 인코딩하며, 모델 출력을 다시 완전하거나 스트리밍된 응답으로 파싱합니다. — 사고, 도구 호출, 이미지 및 생성 설정을 포함합니다. 모델 추론, 도구 실행 및 HTTP 전송은 호출자에게 맡겨집니다.

가중치 변환 및 로컬 추론 실행 지침은 inference 폴더를 참조하십시오.

Hi HN,I’ve been working on esp32sim, an open-source ESP32 emulator that runs in the browser.The fun part of the demo is that there is no ESP32 involved — the firmware is executing in the emulator.The goal is to make ESP32 software easier to experiment with, test and simulate without always needing physical hardware connected.Source:
https://github.com/mikroverk/esp32simI made a short video showing it in action:
https://youtu.be/waoWFilTWEcI’m particularly interested in feedback from embedded developers: what would an emulator like this need to support before you’d actually use it for development, testing or CI?

items.title: Meta shakes up the frontiers, open and closed
items.body:
This has been a week where the balance of American open-weight models took a step change back toward the frontier. Meta took the lead of this charge with Muse Spark Open, which is now the strongest American-made open model by quite some margin, but the addition of Reflection’s first model Beam is also relevant. Without these two models, there would be 20+ open-weight models built and released by Chinese companies better than the best Western models. At the time of writing this, Mistral has also announced a strong model, Mistral Large 4, with an index score of 38 (see below), but its weights are not yet released. There are rumors of a few more strong American open-weight models coming from other organizations too!
In many ways, the gap between the best American and Chinese models has been reduced roughly by half. We’ve gone from the best American open models being largely irrelevant to consumers who require the cutting edge of performance, to them being behind but relevant.

This paints the picture of the cut-throat, competitive nature of the frontier model business. Reflection and Mistral announced their model scores and Meta dropped the weights of a smarter model before these other two labs could get their own weights out. All of these models are competing with Chinese models released months ago, where the industry is collectively asking — where have Kimi and Zhipu AI been since the releases of GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3 on Aug. 18th and Jul. 16th, respectively?
That is a very nuanced question, which I’ll dig into another time. Today’s piece is focused on Meta’s turnaround, what Muse Spark Open means for the ecosystem, and the balance of power across Western frontier labs.
Share
Why Muse Spark Open should take off — and why it may not
One thing we see again and again at Interconnects through our open model analysis is that Western open-weight models get astonishingly more adoption than Chinese models with the same performance-to-size footprint (even though the Chinese models usually come out first)! Muse Spark Open is landing into this environment, at the same time as when open-ended LLM agents are finally real (~GLM 5.2 capabilities and on).
Riding off a rapid increase in performance of Chinese models, the open ecosystem has been living through an acceleration in demand. The inference providers are rapidly scaling, the open post-training economy is forming, and countless enterprises are looking to own their intelligence. Muse Spark Open’s performance falls somewhere above GLM 5.2, near DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and behind GLM 5.3 or Kimi K3. It should be squarely “good enough” to slot right into this.
For some background, from the Muse Spark Open model card on Hugging Face:
Muse Spark Open is an 816B total/42B active parameter open weights model with a context window of 1M tokens. Built for coding and agentic work, Muse Spark Open is natively multimodal. This open weights version has additional safety post-training to make it more robust against misuse as a standalone model without system guardrails. We recommend deploying Muse Spark Open as part of a broader AI system, with additional guardrails suited to the specific use case.

Here’s the distribution of the various Muse models on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.

This is included to loop back to the original model card snippet. It was shared that this open-weight model underwent additional safety training to prepare for this open release. Many observers saw this release as potentially a model that was “broken” during the safety training, as it came out after Muse Spark 1.3.
In reality, this was much more likely a safety tune of Muse Spark 1.2, which would only be a 1 point drop on Artificial Analysis to shore up safety behaviors. When Meta released Muse Glimmer, the 30B agentic model, Alex Wang said that they were preparing to release the Muse Spark 1.2 model as open weights, which fits with the above.
If anything will hold Muse Spark Open back, it’ll be the specific license they designed for it. In summary, this custom license has pretty much all of the restrictive license behaviors we’ve seen (and criticized here) in the last few years of building with open models. They are as follows:
Users of the models in products must display “Built with Muse” on their products. Meta did this with Llama, and Kimi has tried it, but almost no one complies.

There is a revenue-gating factor, where companies that make more than $20M per month across their entire business deploying the model need a separate license with Meta. Other prominent open model providers are doing this too, in order to set up revenue share agreements for re-selling inference.

Muse Spark Open makes you agree to an acceptable use policy, which in the true “open source software” corner of the world makes this model extremely not open-source.

All of the above applies to outputs from the model as well, and derivatives, so there is legal ambiguity if you can safely use the model for synthetic data.

The license does permit using Muse Spark Open for internal research and applications.
We’re at a weird equilibrium where this license is complex and unproven in court, but many players will likely ignore it. Many, many people will build on this model from various inference providers, and Meta will only likely go after egregious violations.
For now, licenses haven’t been the determining factor of AI adoption, but this could change in the future. This is why we think it’s an unnecessary strategic risk for labs trying to compete and regain adoption to have complex, non-standard open licenses for their models.
Interconnects AI is a reader-supported publication. Consider becoming a subscriber.

Is Meta a tier 1 (OpenAI/Anthropic) or tier 2 (Gemini/xAI) frontier lab?
Just a few days before Muse Spark Open, Meta unveiled their closed frontier models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full.1 On traditional benchmarks, these are very strong models only behind Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 and similar to OpenAI’s GPT-6-Astra or Google’s Gemini-4-Argon.
These major releases are coming just over a year out from Meta’s massive AI redirection, characterized by CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s Personal Superintelligence post, which got a lot of criticism at the time. Meta is the only American company with frontier open and closed models. Alibaba’s Qwen has followed a similar strategy, but with a far more open-leaning approach.

The vibe checks across all of these models have been solid, but the expectations were for them to not immediately challenge the level of refinement of the most recent Anthropic and OpenAI models in real-world usage. I’m excited to try them more — time to sign up for another AI subscription.
I like this recent run of form from Meta, driving their own products and directions in the popular Muse agent, taking wins like the leading US open-weight crown when useful. Whether or not it’s financially successful, it’s a unique perspective that fits their history as a business.
It often feels like there’s a revolving door of which lab is nipping at the heels of the Anthropic-OpenAI leading duo. It’s not clear that in the long run Gemini and xAI are out of it, but those two are much more muddled in their offerings than Meta today. If you listen to Zuck and Alexandr Wang on The Cheeky Pint, they clearly had a very specific vision of a high-ownership, high-compute per researcher lab that I would expect to pay off. Many labs die due to layers of bureaucracy and misaligned incentives. Meanwhile Alex Wang has over 200 direct reports — i.e. it’s a very flat org with minimal management — and they’re releasing very consistent model and product improvements.
Leave a comment
Much of my worldview of building models is that you need the resources, the compute, the data, and the talent (all downstream of large sums of money), but organizing them is very hard. Gemini is sometimes described as a place where it’s impossible to get any work done or grow — which is embellishing the issue,
items.body_ko:
이번 주는 미국의 오픈 웨이트 모델 균형이 최전선으로 한 발짝 더 나아간 한 주였습니다. Meta는 Muse Spark Open으로 이 선두를 차지했으며, 이는 이제 상당한 차이로 미국산 오픈 모델 중 가장 강력합니다. 하지만 Reflection의 첫 모델인 Beam의 추가 또한 주목할 만합니다. 이 두 모델이 없었다면, 최고의 서구 모델보다 더 나은 20개 이상의 오픈 웨이트 모델이 중국 기업에 의해 개발 및 출시되었을 것입니다. 이 글을 쓰는 시점에 Mistral도 Mistral Large 4라는 강력한 모델을 발표했으며, 인덱스 점수는 38점(아래 참조)이지만 아직 가중치가 공개되지 않았습니다. 다른 조직에서도 몇몇 강력한 미국 오픈 웨이트 모델이 나올 것이라는 소문도 있습니다!
여러 면에서 최고 수준의 미국 모델과 중국 모델 간의 격차는 대략 절반으로 줄었습니다. 우리는 최고 수준의 성능을 요구하는 소비자에게 대체로 관련성이 없던 최고의 미국 오픈 모델에서, 뒤처지지만 관련성이 있는 모델로 변화했습니다.

이는 최첨단 모델 사업의 치열하고 경쟁적인 특성을 보여줍니다. Reflection과 Mistral은 모델 점수를 발표했고, Meta는 이 두 연구소가 자체 가중치를 공개하기 전에 더 스마트한 모델의 가중치를 공개했습니다. 이 모든 모델은 몇 달 전에 출시된 중국 모델들과 경쟁하고 있으며, 업계는 공동으로 Kimi와 Zhipu AI가 8월 18일과 7월 16일에 각각 GLM-5.3과 Kimi K3를 출시한 이후 어디에 있었는지 묻고 있습니다.
그것은 매우 미묘한 질문이며, 나중에 다시 다룰 것입니다. 오늘 글은 Meta의 전환, Muse Spark Open이 생태계에 의미하는 것, 그리고 서구 최전선 연구소 간의 힘의 균형에 초점을 맞춥니다.
공유
Muse Spark Open이 성공해야 하는 이유 — 그리고 성공하지 못할 수도 있는 이유
Interconnects의 오픈 모델 분석을 통해 우리가 거듭 확인하는 한 가지는 서구 오픈 웨이트 모델이 동일한 성능 대 크기 점유율을 가진 중국 모델(비록 중국 모델이 보통 먼저 출시되더라도!)보다 놀랍도록 더 많은 채택을 얻는다는 것입니다! Muse Spark Open은 이러한 환경에 출시되며, 동시에 개방형 LLM 에이전트가 마침내 현실화되는 시점(~GLM 5.2 기능 등)입니다.
중국 모델의 성능이 급격히 향상됨에 따라 오픈 생태계는 수요의 가속화를 경험하고 있습니다. 추론 제공업체는 빠르게 확장하고 있으며, 오픈 후처리 경제가 형성되고 있고, 수많은 기업들이 자체 인텔리전스를 소유하려고 합니다. Muse Spark Open의 성능은 GLM 5.2보다 약간 높고, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash와 비슷하며, GLM 5.3 또는 Kimi K3보다는 뒤처집니다. 이는 이러한 상황에 적합할 만큼 충분히 “좋을” 것입니다.
배경 설명을 위해 Hugging Face의 Muse Spark Open 모델 카드에서 발췌했습니다:
Muse Spark Open은 1M 토큰의 컨텍스트 창을 가진 총 816B/활성 42B 매개변수 오픈 웨이트 모델입니다. 코딩 및 에이전트 작업을 위해 구축된 Muse Spark Open은 기본적으로 멀티모달입니다. 이 오픈 웨이트 버전은 시스템 가드레일 없이 독립형 모델로서 오용에 대한 견고성을 높이기 위해 추가 안전 후처리 과정을 거쳤습니다. Muse Spark Open을 특정 사용 사례에 적합한 추가 가드레일과 함께 더 넓은 AI 시스템의 일부로 배포하는 것을 권장합니다.

여기에 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index에 있는 다양한 Muse 모델의 분포가 나와 있습니다.

이것은 원래 모델 카드 발췌문으로 돌아가기 위해 포함되었습니다. 이 오픈 웨이트 모델이 오픈 릴리스를 준비하기 위해 추가 안전 훈련을 거쳤다고 공유되었습니다. 많은 관찰자들은 이 릴리스가 Muse Spark 1.3 이후에 나왔기 때문에 안전 훈련 중에 “손상된” 모델일 수 있다고 보았습니다.
실제로는 Muse Spark 1.2의 안전 튜닝이었을 가능성이 훨씬 높으며, 이는 안전 동작을 강화하기 위해 Artificial Analysis에서 1점 하락에 불과할 것입니다. Meta가 30B 에이전트 모델인 Muse Glimmer를 출시했을 때, Alex Wang은 Muse Spark 1.2 모델을 오픈 웨이트로 출시할 준비를 하고 있다고 말했으며, 이는 위와 일치합니다.
Muse Spark Open의 발목을 잡을 것이 있다면, 그들이 설계한 특정 라이선스일 것입니다. 요약하자면, 이 맞춤형 라이선스는 지난 몇 년간 오픈 모델로 구축하면서 우리가 보았던 (그리고 여기에서 비판했던) 제한적인 라이선스 동작을 거의 모두 포함하고 있습니다. 다음과 같습니다:
제품에 모델을 사용하는 사용자는 제품에 “Built with Muse”를 표시해야 합니다. Meta는 Llama로 이를 시도했고, Kimi도 시도했지만 거의 아무도 준수하지 않습니다.

수익 제한 요소가 있습니다. 모델을 배포하여 전체 사업에서 월 2천만 달러 이상을 벌어들이는 회사는 Meta와 별도의 라이선스를 체결해야 합니다. 다른 저명한 오픈 모델 제공업체들도 추론 재판매에 대한 수익 공유 계약을 설정하기 위해 이를 시행하고 있습니다.

Muse Spark Open은 수용 가능한 사용 정책에 동의해야 하며, 진정한 “오픈 소스 소프트웨어” 영역에서는 이 모델을 극히 비오픈 소스로 만듭니다.

위의 모든 사항은 모델의 출력과 파생물에도 적용되므로, 모델을 합성 데이터에 안전하게 사용할 수 있는지에 대한 법적 모호성이 있습니다.

이 라이선스는 Muse Spark Open을 내부 연구 및 응용 프로그램에 사용하는 것을 허용합니다.
우리는 이 라이선스가 복잡하고 법원에서 입증되지 않았지만, 많은 플레이어가 이를 무시할 가능성이 있는 이상한 균형 상태에 있습니다. 많은 사람들이 다양한 추론 제공업체에서 이 모델을 기반으로 구축할 것이며, Meta는 극심한 위반에 대해서만 조치를 취할 가능성이 있습니다.
현재까지 라이선스는 AI 채택의 결정적인 요인이 아니었지만, 미래에는 바뀔 수 있습니다. 이것이 우리가 경쟁하고 채택을 되찾으려는 연구소에 복잡하고 비표준적인 오픈 라이선스가 불필요한 전략적 위험이라고 생각하는 이유입니다.
Interconnects AI는 독자 지원 출판물입니다. 구독자가 되는 것을 고려해 보십시오.

Meta는 티어 1(OpenAI/Anthropic) 또는 티어 2(Gemini/xAI) 최전선 연구소입니까?
Muse Spark Open이 출시되기 며칠 전, Meta는 폐쇄형 최전선 모델인 Muse Wonder와 Muse Wonder Full.1을 공개했습니다. 기존 벤치마크에서 이들은 Anthropic의 Opus 5.5에 이어 매우 강력한 모델이며 Ope와 유사합니다.

items.title: [AINews] High Taste Testers Ep. 1
items.body:
We are piloting a new show on Latent Space: High Taste Testers, a variant of our food show where we pull you in to a typical lunch conversation in San Francisco. All your favorite talking points, starting with Dev Day and going into the latest models and assistants, are here:

Let us know your feedback!

AI News for 10/15/2026-10/16/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews’ website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space. You can opt in/out of email frequencies!

AI Twitter Recap
US Open-Weights Push: Muse Spark Open and Reflection Beam
Muse Spark Open (Meta): An 816B-total, 42B-active MoE with open weights. Artificial Analysis scores it 39 on its Intelligence Index, the highest for a US open-weights model and 13 points above NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Super VL at 26 (AA).
Architecture and footprint: 62 layers, GQA with 16 KV heads, 8 of 256 experts active per token, a 1.8B Perception Encoder and 1M context. Inputs are text, image, video and audio; output is text. BF16 weights are about 1.6TB. Meta’s NVFP4 checkpoint quantizes only the experts, cutting weights to about 530GB. Meta says that fits on 4 Blackwell Ultra GPUs, 8 H200s or two 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios.

Pricing and efficiency: Together, Fireworks and Baseten charge $1.25/$4.25 per M input/output tokens, with $0.15 cached input. AA puts the cost at $0.84 per index task, versus $2.01 for GLM-5.3 and $0.27 for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. It uses 40k output tokens per task, the fewest among the top nine open models (cost). Vals counts 55.5M output tokens across its index, the fewest of any open model, but says input tokens drive most of its cost (Vals).

Weak spot: It ranks last among the top nine open models on AA’s four agentic evals while leading open models on AA-Omniscience. Vals places it #12 among open-weight models and #38 overall (Vals). Arena ranks it the top US open model on Code Arena WebDev with 1511 points, #13 among open models (Arena).

License: The custom Muse Model License requires “Built with Muse Spark Open” attribution. Model-as-a-Service businesses with more than $20M in annual revenue need a separate agreement with Meta.

Ecosystem: mlx-lm had day-0 support with vision, plus an Apple blog post on RDMA-distributed inference across Mac Studios (@zcbenz). vLLM served RL rollouts during Muse training and supports the release at launch (vLLM). SemiAnalysis has added B200 configurations to InferenceX (SemiAnalysis).

Criticism (opinion): @teortaxesTex calls it “DOA” against the smaller, MIT-licensed V4.1 Flash. He also speculates, without evidence, that Meta withheld Spark 1.3 because of distillation from OpenAI (speculation). @alexandr_wang describes MSL as having built “a machine that builds new models.”

Reflection Beam 1.0: A 501B-total, 23B-active MoE with 1M context, released under Apache 2.0. The release includes BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 weights, a DFlash2 drafter, the open Mirror CLI harness Beam was trained on, and a safety report (Reflection, safety report, Mirror).
Independent evals: AA scores it 30, #2 among US open models, using about 26k tokens per task. It reaches 48.5% on AutomationBench-AA but only 3.0% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. On AA-Omniscience it answers 33% correctly but hallucinates at 47% (AA). Arena places it #12 among open models in Agent Arena (±3.84%) and makes it the only non-Chinese model in the top 25 open models on Code WebDev (Arena).

Architecture: Sliding-window attention with a 512 window in a 5:1 pattern, no RoPE, Llama-4-style global attention scaling, gated attention, QK-norm, sandwich norm, logit softcapping and no shared experts (@eliebakouch).

Serving and RL: vLLM had day-0 support. On 4× B300 with NVFP4 at TP4, it measured 1,769 output tok/s at concurrency 16. SkyRL offers day-0 LoRA, full fine-tuning and MXFP8 RL, and reports +62% LoRA decode throughput (276→447 tok/s/GPU), which is a decode result, not an end-to-end training speedup (vLLM, SkyRL). Ollama is serving it free for a limited time, US-hosted with zero data retention (Ollama).

Other open releases: StepFun released Step 5 Preview open weights (Together). Tencent shipped Hy Memory 2.0 and claims Hy-Memory-30B-A3B beats Opus 5 on memory frameworks (Tencent). Datalab released Indra, a 1M-parameter OCR model it says runs 15× faster than Tesseract on CPU (@VikParuchuri).

Frontier Model Rollouts and the Decision-Model Category
Gemini 4 Argon: Now available to Pro subscribers and in AI Studio Build (@_philschmid, AI Studio).
Specs and pricing: The wide release raises the output limit to 1M tokens from 64K, sharing the window with input. Intro pricing is $2/$10 until Nov 30 (DeepLearning.AI).

Results: Perplexity reports a new SOTA on its WANDR research benchmark (@AravSrinivas). Argon ranks #5 in Agent Arena at +13.2% (Arena). @MParakhin gives early praise for its math, with the caveat that it needs higher reasoning effort.

Anthropic speed and price moves: Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10/$0.50 for prompts up to 100K tokens, about 90% cheaper than Haiku 4.5. It scores 39.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 at max effort, versus 16.4% for GPT-6 Luna (DL Weekly). An Opus 5.5 fast mode at 2.5× speed is reported (@kimmonismus). Claude Code now gzips the conversation payload on every turn to cut latency (ClaudeDevs).

OpenAI product updates: GPT-6 Astra Pro in ChatGPT now runs multiple agents on parts of a task in parallel, with faster responses and better tool use (OpenAI). GPT Live 1.1 improves multilingual voice, and nine new presets were recorded with native-speaking actors (@reach_vb, OpenAIDevs). Codex is believed to have one or two new models coming; this is unconfirmed speculation (@kimmonismus).

Elorian Glimpse: A visual-thinking VLM that runs recurrent computation over latent visual states instead of text-only chain of thought.
Claimed results: Elorian says it matches or beats Astra on 5 of 12 benchmarks at 17× lower token prices, trained on “hundreds of GPUs” (@dustinvtran).

Informal test: @omarsar0 found 8 of 10 game boards fully correct, versus 5 of 10 for Gemini 3.8 Flash.

Decision models (calibrated one-pass classifiers):
Liquid d1-ultra: Tops AA’s Decision Index at 65, ahead of Jev 1.14 at 57. Its non-hallucination rate rises to 85% from 2% for d1, but accuracy falls to 32% from 41%. Time per task is 92ms and price is $0.042 per M input tokens, with output free (AA).

Perplexity pplx-decider v1.2: Open weights in a 27B model at 2¢/M and a 4B Flash model at 1¢/M. The update adds reranking, single-pass multi-question inference that is up to 5× faster, and -latest slugs (@AravSrinivas, @denisyarats).

Usage: OpenAI’s Live API added a Decisions API for fast tool delegation (@juberti). In one experiment, swapping Jev into Recursive Language Model sub-calls was half the cost and 6× faster than Haiku 5.5 on OOLONG at 1M tokens (@Jnatanh).

Inference Hardware and Serving Systems
TPUv7 on AgentX: SemiAnalysis reports 1.42× better perf per dollar than GB300 NVL72 FP4, calculated on an external, non-Google cost basis, and 2.5× versus MI355X (SemiAnalysis).
Interactivity split: TPUv7 is up to 3.16× better than disaggregated GB200 at medium to high interactivity. GB200 FP4 keeps a 1.2× edge at low interactivity (thread). The run was served with vLLM through TorchTPU.

Vera Rubin NVL72 on AA-AgentPerf: Up to 5.7× GB300’s throughput per MW on DeepSeek V4 Pro, falling to 2.8× on Kimi K3, with the largest gains at high per-user speed (AA).
Peak throughput: The gap narrows to 1.14–1.45×. Vera Rubin also posts a record 906 tok/s per user on V4.1 Flash. NVIDIA submitted all of these results.

AMD MI355X: 8× MI355X delivers 24.4% more throughput than HGX B300 on Kimi K3 at 50 tok/s per user, and 87.4% more tokens per dollar (vLLM). Inferact announced a collaboration with AMD to publish open per-model recipes for agentic serving (Inferact).

items.title: Nathan Lambert: Reflecting on Meta’s big week, where US open-weight models now stand, and the outlook for any meanin
items.body:
Reflecting on Meta’s big week, where US open-weight models now stand, and the outlook for any meaningful competition to Anthropic & OpenAI’s models.

Meta feels like they’re going from strength to strength right now, but can they close the last bit of the gap?
